definitions.explanation: The cursive Japanese syllabary, used for native Japanese words and grammatical elements.

examples.japanese: {平仮名|ひらがな}で{書|か}いてください。
{子供|こども}はまず{平仮名|ひらがな}を{習|なら}います。
{平仮名|ひらがな}は46{文字|もじ}あります。
この{漢字|かんじ}を{平仮名|ひらがな}で{読|よ}めますか。
examples.english: Can you read this kanji in hiragana?

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}を{勉強|べんきょう}する{時|とき}は、まず{平仮名|ひらがな}から{始|はじ}めるのが{普通|ふつう}です。
examples.english: When studying Japanese, it's normal to start with hiragana.

notes:
{平仮名|ひらがな} is one of the three main Japanese writing systems. It is the first script most learners study and the foundation of Japanese literacy.

ETYMOLOGY:
{平|ひら} (ordinary, simple) + {仮名|かな} (phonetic script). Developed from simplified cursive forms of {漢字|かんじ}.

JAPANESE WRITING SYSTEMS:
- {平仮名|ひらがな}: cursive syllabary (46 basic characters)
- {片仮名|かたかな}: angular syllabary (for loanwords, emphasis)
- {漢字|かんじ}: Chinese characters (meaning-based)

USES OF HIRAGANA:
- Grammatical particles: は、が、を、に
- Verb and adjective endings ({送|おく}り{仮名|がな})
- Words without standard kanji
- Furigana (reading aids above kanji)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {平仮名|ひらがな}で{書|か}く: to write in hiragana
- {平仮名|ひらがな}{表|ひょう}: hiragana chart
